summary: Grux 0.3.1 sends every labelled secret shorter than 40 characters out in plaintext, behind a test that pinned the leak as correct
description:
**Description**

0.3.1 was a cosmetic release: it fixed label-swallowing, a NAT64 local-use input, and
version signposting. Its one functional change traded that cosmetic complaint for a security
regression.

**Every `NAME=value` secret shorter than 40 characters went out in plaintext.** The generic
entropy pass carries a 40-character floor, and with label handling removed there was nothing
else looking at `NAME=value`. Most real credentials are shorter than 40 characters, so the
practical effect is that labelled secret handling stopped working.

**A test was added that pinned the leak as correct behaviour.** It asserted `redact(s) == s`
against a live-shaped bearer token, so the suite reported green on the leak, and the next
person to fix it would have had to delete an assertion that looked deliberate.

**Impact**

This is the broadest leak in the set. Any `API_KEY=`, `DB_PASSWORD=`, `TOKEN=` or similar
under 40 characters reaches the model provider verbatim.

It scores the same 8.6 as the other credential leaks here, and it is the most dangerous of
them for a reason CVSS has no dial for: **the test suite was green throughout.** Every other
defect in this set could in principle be caught by a caller who wrote a test. This one
shipped with a test asserting the leak was intended.

**Patches**

Fixed in 0.4.0, which replaced the length floor with label recognition: `HF_TOKEN=`,
`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=`, `"api_key":` and friends have their value redacted regardless of
its length or shape. The test that pinned the leak was rewritten in the same release.

**Do not move to 0.4.0**, see Advisory 6. Move to **0.5.0**.

**Workarounds**

None. Padding secrets to 40 characters is not a workaround, it is a coincidence.

**References**

`CHANGELOG.md` sections 0.3.1 and 0.4.0.
